sections.title: Cloud services
sections.subtitle: Modernise, migrate and optimise enterprise cloud environments.

sections.heading: Build a cloud environment that is fit for your business
sections.body:
Workload constraints, migration risk and unclear operating ownership can turn cloud adoption into a new source of cost and fragility. We assess readiness, plan staged migration and agree resilience, security and operating responsibilities before changing the estate.

Baseline cost per workload or transaction, service objectives and recovery requirements. Distinguish the client’s obligations from any managed scope. [Discuss your cloud priorities](#get-in-touch).

sections.heading: What we deliver
sections.description: Workload readiness, engineering and operations with clear responsibilities.

items.title: Readiness and roadmap
items.description: Workload and dependency inventory, disposition decisions and prioritised migration waves with business constraints.

items.title: Landing zones and platform engineering
items.description: Target environment design, identity and access baselines, network controls and deployment configuration.

items.title: Migration and modernisation
items.description: Migration plans, data validation and cutover procedures. Link application refactoring to the modernisation scope.

items.title: Containers and DevOps
items.description: Cluster and deployment baselines where appropriate, automated pipelines, rollout checks and validated rollback procedures.

items.title: Cloud operations and observability
items.description: Monitoring, alerting, failure investigation and runbooks, with named client, provider and service responsibilities.

items.title: Cost and performance optimisation
items.description: Workload cost attribution, usage and performance review, and prioritised changes measured against agreed service objectives.

sections.heading: A secure migration and operating model
sections.description: Illustrative on-premises workload → assessed target and landing zone → migration waves → release gates → operations and optimisation loop.

items.title: 1. Assess and establish foundations
items.description: Map workload dependencies and select a target environment. Agree IAM, network controls, recovery needs and cloud-cost ownership before migration.

items.title: 2. Migrate with controlled releases
items.description: Modernise selected application capabilities and migrate in waves. Validate data and dependent integrations, cutover, service continuity and rollback.

items.title: 3. Operate and optimise
items.description: Monitor workloads, investigate failures and test recovery. Review scaling, performance and spend with accountable operating owners, then prioritise the next change.

sections.heading: Accelerators for cyber-safe cloud delivery
sections.description: Select delivery IP for migration, application engineering and assurance. Agree product fit and reusable versus tailored work during discovery.

items.title: Modernisation and release accelerators
items.description: The Modernisation & Integration Toolkit, Automated Testing & Release Assurance Packs and Cyber-Safe Delivery support the agreed migration and validation scope.

items.title: Linkworks
items.description: Cloud-native solutions, composable UI and REST APIs can support application capabilities where ERP or CRM does not fit; it is not cloud infrastructure.

items.title: testoriumz
items.description: Continuous testing, low-code automation and CI/CD integration can support release assurance for application and integration changes during migration.

sections.note: Products are available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without a Linkfields services engagement. Discovery agrees product fit, reusable accelerator content and client-specific engineering.

sections.heading: From workload assessment to optimised operations

items.description: Assess — Baseline business needs, workloads, dependencies and spend. Client owners confirm the platform scope, service objectives, recovery requirements and migration priorities.
Design — Agree landing zones, IAM, network controls, recovery and cost attribution. Define client, provider and Linkfields responsibilities; security and quality requirements gate the design.
Migrate and validate — Move or modernise workloads in waves. Test data, integrations, cutover, rollback and recovery against agreed acceptance criteria before the client release decision.

Operate and optimise — Transfer monitoring, runbooks and escalation ownership. Measure cost, performance and recovery evidence; agree coverage, exclusions and response/restoration terms for any managed scope.

sections.heading: Acceptance for cutover and operations
sections.body:
Cutover acceptance includes data and integration validation, access-control checks, release evidence and tested rollback and recovery procedures. The client approves remaining risks; operating owners accept monitoring, runbooks and escalation boundaries.

Track workload cost and performance over an agreed period, separating rate discounts and right-sizing from architectural changes. Compare recovery evidence and service performance with agreed objectives—not an unconditional availability or savings promise.

See [Our approach and commercial models](/company/our-approach) for delivery governance and engagement details.

sections.heading: Plan the right engagement
sections.description: Use Time & Materials for readiness and architecture discovery, or Fixed Price for agreed migration waves. A Dedicated Team supports platform engineering; Managed Service covers explicitly agreed cloud operations. Outcome-Based optimisation needs a comparable cost/performance baseline, exclusions and attribution.

items.title: How do we assess workload readiness?
items.description: Review dependencies, data, platform support, usage, spend, security and recovery needs. Agree which workloads to retain, migrate or modernise, and confirm the delivery-platform scope before selecting a target.

items.title: What belongs in a landing zone?
items.description: Agree identity, network, access, logging, deployment and recovery controls for the selected environment. Name ownership and acceptance criteria before workloads are moved.

items.title: Who owns cloud costs and infrastructure?
items.description: Separate cloud-provider accounts and platform charges from Linkfields engineering or managed services. Agree account ownership, cost allocation and approval of changes that affect spend.

items.title: How are recovery and shared responsibility handled?
items.description: Define client, provider and service responsibilities, data recovery requirements and service objectives. Test recovery and rollback; any support coverage, response/restoration terms and exclusions must be agreed.

items.title: What should we bring to the conversation?
items.description: Share the workload estate, current platforms, migration goals, cost and resilience constraints, and support needs. We can agree discovery access, confidentiality and delivery scope.
